As a movie, Project X is honestly kind of ass. It's not really an enjoyable experience, especially around the start and end. The camerawork is shoddy, and while that's deliberate, it really doesn't do any favours. The characters are quite flat and annoying in many ways. I didn't really enjoy it general. However, this movie stands as a monument to late pre-internet American high school and it stands tall. No other media I've ever seen set in such a scene has ever reached the heights of representation that Project X does. It's nostalgic, in a sense. Of its time in the best way.

I was 21 when this came out. Why didn't I watch this in my 20s? Would've been an interesting starting point. Anyway, fun all in all, but it's missing the heart and soul you get in many of these highschool movies. Drax is somewhat of an intriguing character, but the rest just gets tiring after a while. I feel like they could do much more with the video camera, making it feel much more raw and authentic. It's dumb, and it's supposed to be dumb, but even as a movie it tries to hard. Did I perhaps watch it at the wrong age?

Much like the party that Costa throws for Tommy, Project X seems determined to be the big, explosive, definitive conclusion to the “one crazy party” sub-genre of comedy. It has everything that could possibly excite a heterosexual teenage boy in the early 2010s – alcohol, drugs, boobs, stunts, implied sex, and everything in between. And for the most part, its mission is successful; later movies that delve into this sandbox, like Office Christmas Party , don’t quite have their hearts in the same place, and it comes off feeling more tired than energetic. My feelings on Project X are actually pretty similar to Office Christmas Party – the debauchery is hardly engaging, and since that’s what the whole film is supposedly barreling towards, it has to be pretty compelling to break through. At least Project X has the excuse of solely focusing on the party. I am not exaggerating when I say there is nothing more to this film than the insanity and excess that comes from an out-of-control hormonal rager. Most of the characters are irredeemably annoying, but that’s nothing new for a film of this caliber. Their values (which, as far as I can tell, bear little difference from the movie as a whole) feel antiquated, even for 2012. It may have intentionally provided an apex (which, in turn, may have killed the sub-genre), but that doesn’t quite dovetail with the quality of the movie itself, as hard as it tries to make itself stand out. It doesn’t matter how cool you were or weren’t in high school; the shenanigans in Project X are more exhausting than anything else.

Les fils de bourges de Pasadena s'amusent à tout faire péter dans leur banlieue chic lors d'un anniversaire. Fin de l'histoire. C'est sympa par moment, surtout quand Costa ne parle pas. J'avais un souvenir plus créatif dans la destruction. C'est assez répétitif au final. Mais alors la fin... Cauchemar. Le père du héros devra tout rembourser mais dans son regard on peut voir qu'il est fier que son fils se soit surpassé. Fierté masculine quand tu nous tiens. Une belle leçon de vie. Costa, l'insupportable red flag sur patte, s'en sort grâce aux avocats de ses parents blindés, lui permettant ainsi de rester le fdp qu'il est en plein air. Avoir plein d'argent me permet de ne rien assumer ni d'apprendre de mes actes. Une bien belle morale.
